title: Algebra I
description: Algebra for non-majors: sets and functions, relations and orderings, an introduction to number theory, groups, rings and fields, matrices and determinants, and linear systems, eigenvalues and vector spaces. Built from the MAT 213 lecture notes (Algebra I, B. O. Onasanya, University of Ibadan) and their chapter files in the course folder.

topics.title: Sets and Functions
topics.summary: A set is a collection of elements, compared by subset and equality and combined by union, intersection, complement, difference and symmetric difference. Partitions split a set into disjoint blocks, and functions may be injective, surjective or bijective.
subtopics: Sets, cardinality and the empty set
Subsets, proper subsets and the universal set
Set operations and symmetric difference
Cartesian products and partitions
Functions: domain, codomain and image
Injective, surjective and bijective functions; composition

topics.title: Relations, Equivalence and Orderings
topics.summary: A relation on a set may be reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric or transitive; equivalence relations partition a set into equivalence classes. A partial order makes a POSET, which may be a chain or well ordered and has first, last, minimal and maximal elements.
subtopics: Relations, inverse relations and relations on a set
Reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric and transitive
Equivalence relations and congruence modulo m
Equivalence classes and the quotient set
Partial orders, POSETs and chains
First, last, minimal, maximal and well ordered

topics.title: Introduction to Number Theory
topics.summary: The integers have ordered and divisibility properties; every integer from 2 up factors uniquely into primes. The Euclidean algorithm gives gcd(a, b) and integers u, v with d = au + bv, which solve linear congruences in the residue classes Zₘ.
subtopics: Properties of (Z, +) and (Z, ·)
Divisibility, primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic
The division (Euclidean) algorithm
GCD, LCM and d = au + bv
Modular arithmetic, residue classes and Euler's phi function
Solving congruence equations

topics.title: Algebraic Systems and Groups
topics.summary: A binary operation on a set may be closed, commutative, associative or distributive, with identities and inverses. Groupoids, semigroups and monoids lead to groups; cyclic groups, subgroups, homomorphisms and symmetric groups follow.
subtopics: Binary operations and their properties
Identity and inverse elements
Groupoid, semigroup and monoid
Groups, abelian groups and cyclic groups
Order of a group and of an element; subgroups and Lagrange
Homomorphisms and the symmetric group Sₙ

topics.title: Rings, Integral Domains and Fields
topics.summary: A ring has two operations: it is an abelian group under addition and a semigroup under multiplication, with distributivity. Zero divisors, integral domains, characteristic, subrings, division rings and fields refine the idea.
subtopics: Definition of a ring
Examples: Z, mZ, Zₘ, R[x], Z[i] and matrices
Commutative and unital rings
Zero divisors and integral domains
Characteristic and subrings
Division rings and fields

topics.title: Matrices and Determinants
topics.summary: Matrices over a field have transposes and special forms such as symmetric and orthogonal. Elementary row operations give the row reduced echelon form and the rank, and determinants, cofactors and adjoints give the inverse.
subtopics: Types of matrix: square, row, column
Transpose; symmetric, skew-symmetric, normal and orthogonal
Matrix addition and multiplication
Elementary row operations and elementary matrices
Row reduced echelon form and rank
Determinants, cofactors, adjoint and the inverse

topics.title: Linear Systems, Eigenvalues and Vector Spaces
topics.summary: Systems AX = B are homogeneous or not and are classified by the ranks of A and [A | B]. Eigenvalues are roots of the characteristic polynomial, with the Cayley-Hamilton theorem and diagonalisation; vector spaces, bases and linear transformations generalise these ideas.
subtopics: Homogeneous and non-homogeneous systems
Consistency from ranks
Characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors
The Cayley-Hamilton theorem and similar matrices
Vector spaces, linear combinations, independence and bases
Linear transformations, kernel, nullity and rank
